answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by forcing each identity to climb a public terrace of bonded, time-locked work before its votes or payouts count at full weight. New keys start at the bottom: only after a crystal-clear trail of peer-verified jobs matures does reputation unlock higher tiers. A farm can spin up a thousand empty names, but each one still faces the same canyon of unproven history, and cheap clones never reach the level where influence is actually priced.
